questions.stem: How are elements arranged in the modern Periodic Table?

options.text: In order of increasing relative atomic mass
In order of increasing atomic number

questions.explanation: The modern Periodic Table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number (number of protons). This was established after Moseley's work corrected Mendeleev's original ordering by atomic mass.

questions.stem: What is a 'group' in the Periodic Table?

options.text: A vertical column of elements with similar properties
A set of elements with the same mass number

questions.explanation: A group is a vertical column in the Periodic Table. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer shell electrons and therefore similar chemical properties.

questions.stem: What does the period number tell you about an element's electronic structure?

options.text: The number of outer shell electrons
The number of occupied electron shells

questions.explanation: The period number tells you how many electron shells are occupied. For example, elements in Period 3 have electrons in three shells.

questions.stem: Why do elements in the same group have similar chemical properties?

options.text: They have the same number of protons
They have the same number of electron shells
They have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
They have the same total number of electrons

questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of outer shell electrons. Since chemical reactions involve outer shell electrons, these elements react in similar ways.

questions.stem: Where are metals generally found in the Periodic Table?

options.text: On the left-hand side and in the centre

questions.explanation: Metals are found on the left-hand side and in the centre of the Periodic Table, while non-metals are found on the right-hand side. A staircase line roughly separates them.

questions.stem: An element is in Group 1 and Period 3. How many electrons does it have in its outer shell?
questions.explanation: The group number tells you the number of outer shell electrons. An element in Group 1 has 1 electron in its outer shell. This element is sodium (Na).

questions.stem: What are elements called that have properties of both metals and non-metals?
questions.explanation: Metalloids (or semi-metals) are elements found along the boundary between metals and non-metals in the Periodic Table. They have properties of both, such as silicon and germanium.
